subject.title: fix(active-memory): bound legacy toggle migration reads

question: Should `openclaw doctor` treat an oversized retired Active Memory toggle file as a recoverable skipped migration—retaining the file and requiring operator remediation—in exchange for preventing unbounded memory use?
rationale: The implementation is technically bounded and non-destructive, but choosing the permanent upgrade behavior for legacy user opt-outs is a compatibility decision rather than a mechanical code correction.

options.title: Accept bounded skip recovery
options.body: Merge the 8 MiB bounded-read behavior, retaining oversized legacy sources and warning operators to resolve them before retrying migration.

options.title: Require an alternate migration path
options.body: Keep the PR open until the migration can safely handle larger supported legacy payloads without buffering them unboundedly.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded skip recovery
recommendation.body: Merge the 8 MiB bounded-read behavior, retaining oversized legacy sources and warning operators to resolve them before retrying migration.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the current implementation context, while current-main feature-history ownership was not independently recoverable during this review.
